content: 1. Cobicistat and Imatinib: Cobicistat increases the plasma levels and effects of imatinib by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme involved in its hepatic and intestinal metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised during coadministration. 2. Atazanavir and Imipramine: Atazanavir raises the levels and effects of imipramine through an unspecified interaction mechanism, likely involving CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Cobicistat and Imipramine: Cobicistat enhances the levels and effects of imipramine through mechanisms requiring further clarification. Dose titration and close monitoring are necessary when coadministered with tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) and cobicistat. 4. Atazanavir and Indinavir: Atazanavir increases the levels and effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs may elevate the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are required. 5. Isoniazid and Cobicistat: Isoniazid raises the levels and effects of cobicistat by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Atazanavir and Insulin Aspart: Atazanavir reduces the effects of insulin aspart, potentially due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Hyperglycemia has been reported. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 7. Atazanavir and Insulin Degludec: Atazanavir decreases the effects of insulin degludec through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Protease inhibitors may induce new-onset diabetes mellitus (DM), exacerbate existing DM, or cause hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. 8. Atazanavir and Insulin Detemir/Glargine/Glulisine/Inhaled Lispro/NPH/Regular Human Insulin: Atazanavir reduces the effects of these insulin formulations, likely due to insulin resistance. Hyperglycemia has been reported with protease inhibitors. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 9. Isoniazid and Atazanavir: Isoniazid increases the levels and effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Cobicistat and Isradipine: Cobicistat raises the levels and effects of isradipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 11. Istradefylline and Atazanavir: Istradefylline increases the levels and effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. When coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, the istradefylline dose should not exceed 20 mg/day. 12. Cobicistat and Istradefylline: Cobicistat enhances the levels and effects of istradefylline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 13. Atazanavir and Ivacaftor: Atazanavir increases the levels and effects of ivacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of ivacaftor is recommended when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 14. Cobicistat and Ivacaftor: Cobicistat raises the levels and effects of ivacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 15. Atazanavir and Ixabepilone: Atazanavir increases the levels and effects of ixabepilone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 16. Cobicistat and Ketoconazole: Cobicistat and ketoconazole mutually increase each other's levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 17. Atazanavir and Ketamine: Atazanavir decreases the levels and effects of ketamine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 18. Atazanavir and Labetalol: Atazanavir enhances the effects of labetalol through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of hypotension, bradycardia, atrioventricular (AV) block, and prolonged PR interval. Consider lowering the beta-blocker dose. 19. Atazanavir and Lacosamide: Atazanavir increases the levels and effects of lacosamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 20. Atazanavir and Lamivudine: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are advised. 21. Atazanavir and Lamotrigine: Atazanavir decreases the levels and effects of lamotrigine by increasing its metabolism. This interaction is more clinically significant with ritonavir-boosted atazanavir than with unboosted atazanavir. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 22. Cobicistat and Lansoprazole: Cobicistat increases the levels and effects of lansoprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 23. Atazanavir and Lapatinib: Atazanavir raises the levels and effects of lapatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 24. Lenacapavir and Atazanavir: Lenacapavir increases the levels and effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with atazanavir/cobicistat or atazanavir/ritonavir should be avoided. Use with atazanavir alone may be considered with caution. 25. Cobicistat and Letermovir: Cobicistat increases the levels of letermovir by reducing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 26. Atazanavir and Levamlodipine: Atazanavir increases the levels and effects of levamlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 27. Atazanavir and Levofloxacin: Atazanavir enhances the effects of levofloxacin through pharmacodynamic synergy. Caution and monitoring are advised. 28. Cobicistat and Levonorgestrel: Cobicistat increases the levels and effects of levonorgestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use of a nonhormonal contraceptive is recommended. 29. Atazanavir and Lidocaine: Atazanavir increases the levels and effects of lidocaine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical monitoring is recommended when coadministered with antiarrhythmics. 30. Atazanavir and Linagliptin: Atazanavir increases the levels and effects of linagliptin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 31. Atazanavir and Liraglutide: Atazanavir reduces the effects of liraglutide, potentially due to insulin resistance. Hyperglycemia has been reported with protease inhibitors. Caution and monitoring are advised. 32. Atazanavir and Lofepramine: Atazanavir increases the levels of lofepramine through an unspecified mechanism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 33. Atazanavir and Lopinavir: Atazanavir raises the levels and effects of lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 34. Atazanavir and Loratadine: Atazanavir increases the levels and effects of loratadine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 35. Cobicistat and Losartan: Cobicistat increases the levels and effects of losartan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised.
